h: Hats, Downs and Bedfordshire Days Out
p: Luton's football club is nicknamed the Hatters, and there's a good reason for it. The town was once the centre of the British hat-making trade, especially straw hats, and you can still spot traces of that heritage around the old Hat District near the town centre. It's a fun bit of history to share with the kids on the way home.

For your Gravity visit, a little prep makes things easier. Book your slot in advance, sort the waiver online, and bring water and a towel. Wear comfortable clothes, take off any jewellery and keep valuables secure. Grip socks can often be reused, so bring them back next time and save a few quid.

If you want to see a bit more of Bedfordshire, Dunstable Downs is just outside Luton and offers big skies, great walks and the chance to watch gliders soaring overhead from the nearby gliding club. ZSL Whipsnade Zoo sits close by on the edge of the Chilterns and is a brilliant day out, with large paddocks and lots of animals to see.

Over at Silsoe, Wrest Park, run by English Heritage, has formal gardens, statues and a grand French-style house to explore. Closer to home, Wardown Park is a pleasant spot for a stroll by the lake. Between them, they make Luton a handy base for a busy weekend of family fun.
